trigger_condition: interpolate returns undefined or NaN for an invalid/unsupported hex string
potential_consequence: blendColorsHex returns '#000000' silently; deriveContrastGray receives wrong background, yields wrong contrast gray

trigger_condition: contrastTarget <= 1.0 passed to deriveContrastGray (e.g. caller passes wrong constant)
guard_snippet: if (contrastTarget <= 1) return '128 128 128'; // degenerate — no gray can satisfy ratio < 1
potential_consequence: lTarget formula produces NaN or negative; channel clamps to 0, emitting '0 0 0' regardless of background

guard_snippet: lBg < DARK_BG_LUMINANCE_THRESHOLD uses strict-less; verify the boundary case produces valid contrast against #2e2e2e-ish backgrounds
potential_consequence: Off-by-one at the luminance flip point may darken when lightening is needed, producing contrast below 4.5:1

trigger_condition: navigationTextColor is identical to navigationBackground (zero-contrast text, blended color == background)
guard_snippet: blendColorsHex with fg==bg always equals bg; deriveContrastGray still runs correctly — verify no special case needed
potential_consequence: Surface var computed against background color directly; may produce unintended hover pill color when text is invisible

trigger_condition: Two rules independently blend the same (navigationTextColor, navigationBackground, BOTTOM_NAV_LABEL_ALPHA) triple
guard_snippet: Share a single blended intermediate variable (or a combined rule) so a future alpha change updates both atomically
potential_consequence: Alpha changed in one blend but not the other makes text and surface derived from different effective colors, breaking contrast guarantee

trigger_condition: rgbChannels string with fractional numbers (e.g. '254.7 0 0') passed to relativeLuminance — .map(Number) parses floats correctly but the channel formula was designed for 0-255 integers
guard_snippet: const channel = (c: number) => { const s = c / 255; ... } — add assertion that input is 0-255 range or parse with Math.round
potential_consequence: Non-integer channels silently produce a slightly wrong luminance; test may pass or fail inconsistently near the 4.5 boundary

trigger_condition: Tests only cover pure black and pure white navigationBackground; saturated mid-range backgrounds (e.g. #7c3aed) are untested
guard_snippet: Add a third test case with a saturated mid-range background where the old isDarkColor heuristic and new contrast formula may diverge
potential_consequence: Contrast failure on saturated backgrounds goes undetected; regression reachable by any custom theme with a colored nav background

trigger_condition: isDarkColor removed from rules.ts imports but still exported and used by other callers
guard_snippet: Verify no remaining call sites in rules.ts; the export itself is harmless but an orphaned import warning may indicate missed usage
potential_consequence: If any sibling rule still indirectly relied on the same dark/light bifurcation, behavior silently changes
